prize_parts.citation: For energy-landscape theory of protein folding and its experimental mapping of folding pathways and transition states

statement.case_for: Energy-landscape theory gave protein folding a physical formulation: a funneled, minimally frustrated landscape resolves Levinthal's paradox and connects statistical mechanics to measurable kinetics. Fersht's phi-value analysis, built on protein engineering and kinetics, made transition states experimentally visible, so the prize would honour a theory together with the experiments that tested it, which is what I look for in a mechanism stated in physical terms. The picture has decades of independent confirmation from simulation and kinetics, and it underlies how the community now thinks about structure prediction and design. The 2024 prize rewarded predicting and designing structures, not explaining why folding works, so I do not see it as redundant. The attribution is also comparatively compact: Wolynes and Onuchic for the funnel and Fersht for the experimental basis.
statement.case_against: Credit in the theory is shared. Bryngelson, Dill and others have real priority claims, and the three-name limit excludes at least two people whose work is in the credited set. A critic could say the prize rests on a line of work rather than one attributable discovery, and that the funnel is more a unifying conceptual picture than a single decisive result. Its opening support is also narrow: one first place and two top-three rankings. The 2024 prize touches the same territory and may lead colleagues to see folding as already honoured.

responses.point: Linke ranks biomolecular phase separation first (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation with quantitative support and wide reach, while noting that the in-vivo relevance of many condensates is still debated.
responses.response: I share the appeal of a physics-based principle, and I put B022 among my alternatives. Our difference is maturity and attribution. The folding funnel has been tested for decades against kinetics and simulation. For condensates, the founding observation (P granules) and the in-vitro phase behaviour are secure, but the question of what condensates do in cells, and which are truly phase-separated, remains open, as Heiner concedes. I would also want the expert reports to say how the credit divides between the founding observation and the quantitative grammar, with Pappu and Mittag left out. I would wait on B022 rather than rank it above B027.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks targeted protein degradation first as a new pharmacological principle, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as a defensible three, while admitting that no PROTAC is approved and that the cereblon/glue strand crowds the name limit.
responses.response: I agree that induced proximity is conceptually novel and I keep B068 as an alternative. Johan's own caveats are the ones that concern me. The prize would be split between the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs, and Handa, Ito, Sakamoto and Gray cannot all fit. I would also want the expert reports to separate chemical insight from drug-development momentum before the committee decides on a modality that has no approved drug yet. If the committee insists on this field, I would tie the citation to the mechanism of degradation, not to the clinical pipeline.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation first and also places energy-landscape theory third, describing it as a prime example of reducing a complex biological problem to thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, and she notes that the 2024 prize touched adjacent territory.
responses.response: Emma and I agree on the substance, and her support is welcome since it is one of the few places where our rankings overlap. On the 2024 overlap, I would say that the earlier prize was about predicting and designing structure with machine learning and computation, while the funnel explains why sequences fold at all, so the two are complementary. I do take her point that Bryngelson and Dill have claims. I would not reopen the trio unless the reports show that the minimal-frustration principle has a different origin than Wolynes and Onuchic.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first, calling it a general method with clear ligand-design novelty and decades of industrial use, while recognising that Kosugi's tin-amide precedent and the 2010 cross-coupling prize may count against it.
responses.response: I accept that B057 is mature and has a clear two-person attribution, and it is a serious alternative to what I propose. My reservation is about the argument that its impact is obvious, not about its quality. Widespread use in medicinal chemistry shows the method is valuable, but in the committee's terms I want to know how much new chemical understanding it gave beyond the 2010 palladium coupling work. If the expert reports show that the ligand-controlled mechanistic advance is itself fundamental, I could support it as a second prize part, though I have not placed it among my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether Bryngelson or Dill should displace one of the three proposed names, which depends on the expert reports on priority for the funneled-landscape and minimal-frustration ideas.
How much the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design reduces appetite for another protein-folding prize.
Whether the committee prefers a single-achievement prize or a two-part configuration, since B027 is not the broadest-supported candidate at present.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B027, B022 or B068; none of the credited names appears in my profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou and a long-time colleague of Johan Aqvist, but this does not bear on the shortlisted candidates.
